_why: PLA-8 batch 23 (roots). Ids PINNED BEFORE FAN-OUT (batch 17's lesson: zero drift). Every id below was decided against the live roster with a STEMMED token-subset scan (not equality -- batch 22 missed two with an equality check) plus a TAXON CHECK read from each crop's own prose. Authoring agents MUST use these verbatim and MUST NOT mint their own.
_scan: 216 distinct live problem ids over 775 id-bearing problems, canonical b118f19d.

pests.name: Carrot rust fly
pests.evidence: EXACT-STEM x3 (carrot, celery, parsley), all Apiaceae; same Chamaepsila rosae host range.

pests.name: Leafminers
pests.evidence: No bare `leafminer` id exists; all four live ones are crop-prefixed AND SINGULAR (allium-, beet-spinach-, celery-, citrus-leafminer). Parsnip's prose names no genus, so a genus-bearing id would overclaim.

pests.name: Aster leafhopper (aster yellows vector)
pests.evidence: cosmos carries `aster-leafhoppers` for the same insect in the same vector role. Roster form is plural; parsnip's display name is singular. Id follows the roster, not the name.

diseases.name: Itersonilia canker (parsnip canker)
diseases.evidence: No stem-level subset or superset anywhere on the roster.
diseases.type_evidence: Itersonilia perplexans, a fungus. CORRECTED 2026-09-01: this line first read 'Itersonilia pastinacae', which I asserted rather than read; parsnip's own prose names I. perplexans in both registers. Caught by the authoring agent. The type is fungal on either reading, so nothing was blocked.

diseases.name: Aster yellows
diseases.evidence: EXACT-STEM x5 including carrot; same phytoplasma, same vector.
diseases.type_evidence: ROSTER UNANIMOUS x5 -- phytoplasma is typed bacterial, NOT viral. Do not re-derive.

diseases.name: Damping-off
diseases.evidence: EXACT-STEM x13 including carrot. Do NOT use `root-rots-damping-off` (x3), which is a WIDER compound problem.

pests.name: Colorado potato beetle
pests.evidence: EXACT-STEM x1 (eggplant); Leptinotarsa decemlineata, same insect.

pests.name: Flea beetles
pests.evidence: EXACT-STEM x32, the dominant roster form. Do NOT copy swiss-chard's singular `flea-beetle` -- that is a KNOWN open one-token repoint (roots handoff section 6), not a precedent to spread.

pests.name: Aphids and the viruses they spread
pests.evidence: Bare `aphids` (x59) names a FEEDING pest; potato's entry says outright 'Virus pressure, not the feeding itself, is the main reason to manage them' and turns on PVY/leafroll and certified seed. A shorter roster id would name a narrower problem.
pests.type_evidence: sits in pests[]; the ORGANISM is the aphid. cf. bare `aphids` x59 insect. The viral half is the consequence, not the type.

pests.name: Wireworms
pests.evidence: EXACT-STEM x1 (radish); click beetle larvae, prose matches radish's closely.

diseases.name: Late blight
diseases.evidence: Phytophthora infestans, identical to the 6 tomato-crop precedents; potato's own prose says it infects both. NOTE celery also holds `late-blight` for Septoria apiicola -- its own prose flags the unrelatedness. That is a PRE-EXISTING collision, not one this batch creates, and ids are per-crop join keys.

diseases.name: Early blight
diseases.evidence: EXACT-STEM x7; potato's prose names Alternaria solani, the same pathogen as the tomato precedents.

diseases.name: Common scab
diseases.evidence: TAXON CHECK PASSES EXPLICITLY: beet's own prose says Streptomyces scabies is 'the same organism that causes potato scab'. beet/common-scab also just gained even_watering + lower_soil_ph in the thin-ladder backfill, which is the control set potato scab needs.
diseases.type_evidence: roster unanimous x1 (beet); Streptomyces is a bacterium

diseases.name: Blackleg and bacterial soft rot
diseases.evidence: TAXON CHECK FAILS on reuse: live `blackleg` (cabbage, kohlrabi) is the FUNGUS Phoma lingam / Leptosphaeria maculans; potato's is BACTERIA in Pectobacterium. Different kingdom, same word. Compound-id precedent: root-rots-damping-off, dried-fruit-beetle-souring, cane-canker-dieback.
diseases.type_evidence: Pectobacterium (prose). NOTE live `blackleg` is typed FUNGAL because the brassica one IS a fungus -- another face of the same collision.

pests.name: Sweet potato weevil
pests.evidence: No stem-level subset or superset on the roster.

pests.name: Wireworms and root-feeding beetle larvae
pests.evidence: radish's `wireworms` is click beetle larvae ALONE. Sweet potato's entry explicitly widens to a complex: 'The same root-scarring complex includes larvae of spotted and banded cucumber beetles (Diabrotica) and flea beetles (Systena)'. Reusing the bare id would narrow a compound problem.

pests.name: Flea beetles
pests.evidence: EXACT-STEM x32. NOTE: this is the FOLIAR entry; Systena flea beetle LARVAE appear inside wireworms-root-feeding-larvae. Keep the two ladders distinct -- do not cross-write root controls onto the foliar entry.

pests.name: Whiteflies and the viruses they spread
pests.evidence: Bare `whiteflies` (x5, e.g. english-cucumber) is a FEEDING entry about populations building under cover. Sweet potato's says 'Virus pressure, not the feeding itself, is the main reason' and turns on feathery mottle / leaf curl virus and certified slips. Deliberately parallel to potato's aphids-virus-vectors.
pests.type_evidence: sits in pests[]; cf. bare `whiteflies` x5 insect

diseases.name: Fusarium wilt (stem rot)
diseases.evidence: Fusarium oxysporum, the same species as all 8 precedents. Each precedent carries its own forma specialis (spinach names f. sp. spinaciae); sweet potato names the species bare. Same-species-different-f.sp. is the established roster pattern for this id.

diseases.name: Root-knot nematode
diseases.evidence: EXACT-STEM x4 (carrot, fig, okra, swiss-chard); Meloidogyne spp.

diseases.name: Black rot
diseases.evidence: TAXON CHECK FAILS on reuse: live `black-rot` (x10, all brassicas) is the BACTERIUM Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris; sweet potato's is the FUNGUS Ceratocystis fimbriata. Different kingdom, same words. Crop-prefix precedent: carrot-leaf-blight, citrus-brown-rot, bee-balm-rust, sunflower-rust.

diseases.name: Scurf and storage soft rot
diseases.evidence: No stem-level subset or superset on the roster.
diseases.type_evidence: MIXED and flagged for the read: scurf is Monilochaetes infuscans (fungus) and leads the entry; the storage soft rots are "bacteria and fungi (including Rhizopus)". Typed on the named lead organism. Either fungal or bacterial reaches disease_general, so cure_and_store is legal on both readings.

_types_note: type is PINNED TOO. Every REUSED id inherits a roster-UNANIMOUS type (measured, not assumed). All 22 source records carry the coarse type 'pest'/'disease'; this is the uniform coarse -> fine upgrade the roots handoff specified.
